correctness.rationale: Exactly reconstructed the graph Čech nerve from [1, Lemma 2.2], all 475 odd-scale simplices and 1,770 Hasse covers; certified 219 disjoint matching pairs and a complete topological ordering of the reversed-incidence DAG, leaving one 0-cell and 36 3-cells. Forman yields the integral 36-sphere wedge. Forty scale-two elementary free-pair deletions leave the embedded Petersen graph and preserve the H1 persistence map. The graph diameter two gives the full simplex at scale four. An independent GF(2) chain-rank calculation gives (9,36,84,75,15), agreeing with predicted ranks, without being used as a substitute for integral homotopy.

originality.rationale: The general odd-scale Čech facet lemma [1] applies, but the proved special-case theorems of [1] are for hypercube graphs, not Petersen. The earlier Petersen D-neighborhood calculation [2] supplies scale-two H1 but does not imply the 36 three-sphere odd-scale nerve. Discrete-Morse matching, acyclicity, and persistence ranks for the new complex are not consequences of the checked primary claims or the distinct published Petersen cut/matching results. Three alias/parameter searches and historical deduplication identified no dominating statement. Residual unindexed equivalence risk is acknowledged.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently named computation of the same edge-union nerve might exist.
The finite discrete-Morse verification is self-contained and reproducible but has not undergone independent external audit.

value.rationale: The odd threshold three for the canonical Petersen graph is the first nontrivial graph Čech scale outside the girth-controlled recovery interval and determines a natural, presently otherwise uncovered homotopy invariant. The full integral barcode records the precise transition from six 1-cycles to 36 3-sphere classes; this is not recoverable from the older vertex-centered D-neighborhood table, and is materially informative for graph Čech topology.
